draft.title: Biofuels from fermentation
card: A biofuel is a fuel made from living material, such as plants. Plant material contains sugars, or starch and cellulose that can be broken down into sugars.
In fermentation, microbes such as yeast break down sugars without oxygen. Yeast makes ethanol and carbon dioxide, and releases a small amount of energy for its own use.
The ethanol is separated from the mixture, often by distillation, and used as a fuel. It can be blended with petrol.
Sugar cane, corn and wheat are common sources. Fermentation needs anaerobic conditions, so the vessel is sealed from air. With oxygen, yeast would respire aerobically and make little ethanol.
draft.remember: Biofuel ethanol comes from microbes fermenting plant sugars without oxygen.

a.q: Why is the vessel used to ferment sugar cane juice into ethanol kept sealed from air?
opts: Yeast makes ethanol only when oxygen is absent
Yeast needs oxygen to make ethanol from sugars
Oxygen would turn the ethanol into plant starch
Air would stop the sugar cane juice from dissolving
a.why: Ethanol is made by anaerobic fermentation, so oxygen must be kept out. With oxygen, yeast would respire aerobically and make little ethanol. Oxygen does not turn ethanol into starch.
a.clue: Think about which type of respiration makes ethanol.

b.q: Ben's company in Queensland ferments waste sugar cane juice in open tanks that let in plenty of air. The ethanol yield is low. What is the best explanation?
opts: Yeast respires aerobically, so less ethanol is made
Yeast stops using sugar once air reaches the tanks
Air makes the yeast produce lactic acid, not ethanol
Oxygen in the tanks is turned into carbon dioxide only
b.why: With oxygen present, yeast uses aerobic respiration, which releases more energy and makes mostly carbon dioxide and water, not ethanol. Lactic acid is the animal product of anaerobic respiration, so it is not made by yeast here.
b.clue: Which type of respiration does yeast use when oxygen is available?

a.best: Yeast makes ethanol only when oxygen is absent

b.best: Yeast respires aerobically, so less ethanol is made

problems.detail: The right option says yeast makes ethanol 'only' when oxygen is absent. The card says that with oxygen, yeast makes 'little ethanol', not none. In reality, yeast can still ferment in air when sugar is high (the Crabtree effect). Better: 'Yeast makes much more ethanol when oxygen is absent.'
